title: 6 Things God Does Before Elevation
paragraphs: 6 Things God Does Before Elevation
There is a version of you that God cannot trust with elevation yet.
Not because He hates you.
Not because He forgot you.
Not because your prayers are being ignored.
But because elevation without transformation destroys people.
Some people are praying for platforms while God is still trying to heal their pride.
Some are begging for influence while secretly addicted to validation.
Some want visibility while still spiritually collapsing in private.
And what terrifies heaven is not your weakness.
It is the possibility of giving you something your soul is not prepared to survive.
That is why Scripture repeatedly shows a painful pattern.
Before God elevates a person… He first breaks them. Purifies them. Strips them. Tests them. Hides them. And teaches them how to walk with Him when nobody is clapping.

Joseph wore chains before robes. David lived in caves before palaces. Moses wandered deserts before deliverance. Peter wept bitterly before preaching boldly. Paul lost everything before changing the world.
And Jesus Himself walked through wilderness before ministry.
Many believers think delay means denial.
But sometimes delay is mercy.
Because God sees what elevation would expose.
What if the season you hate is actually the season protecting your future?
What if the loneliness is creating dependency on God?
What if the silence is teaching you discernment?
What if the crushing is creating oil?
Be honest. Some of you are exhausted because God is dismantling a version of you that cannot follow Him into the next season.
Because this article may explain the season you are surviving right now.
1. God Exposes Hidden Idols Before Elevation
One of the most dangerous lies believers tell themselves is this:
“I only need God.”
But suffering reveals what comfort hides.
The Hebrew Scriptures repeatedly reveal that God tests the heart before entrusting greater responsibility.
In Deuteronomy 8:2, Moses tells Israel:
“Remember how the LORD your God led you all the way in the wilderness these forty years, to humble and test you in order to know what was in your heart.”
The Hebrew phrase for “to test you” is:
נַסֹּתְךָ (nasotkha)
It carries the meaning of proving, refining, exposing authenticity.
God already knows what is inside us. The wilderness exposes it to us.
Some people think they are faithful until they lose money.
Some think they trust God until relationships fail.
Some think they love Jesus until obedience becomes costly.
Elevation magnifies whatever already exists inside a person.
That is why God exposes hidden idols before promotion.
Because if He does not destroy your idol in private, your idol will destroy you in public.
Sometimes the idol is not sinful pleasure.
Sometimes the idol is reputation.
Sometimes it is ministry success.
Sometimes it is being needed.
Sometimes it is secretly wanting worship that belongs to God.
The Apostle Paul wrote in Galatians 1:10:
“For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God?”
The Greek word for approval is:
πείθω (peithō)
Meaning: To persuade. To win favor. To seek acceptance.
Many believers are emotionally addicted to human approval while claiming spiritual maturity.
But God will often allow rejection to detox your dependence on people.
Because elevation becomes dangerous when applause becomes oxygen.
Some of you lost relationships because God was confronting the idol of being emotionally worshipped.
Some lost opportunities because God was exposing pride.
Some were isolated because God wanted to reveal that your identity was built on attention instead of intimacy with Him.
And yes… it hurts.
Because God never removes idols gently.
He tears them out.
Like surgery without anesthesia.
But what He removes can no longer enslave you.
2. God Allows Hidden Seasons Before Public Seasons
Nobody likes obscurity.
But heaven loves hiddenness.
Because hidden seasons reveal whether you love God or attention.
David was anointed king in 1 Samuel 16.
But after the oil came obscurity.
Not the throne.
The field.
The sheep.
The silence.
The forgotten place.
Even his own father did not initially believe David was important enough to present before Samuel.
Imagine being overlooked in your own house.
Some of you know exactly what that feels like.
You were faithful.
But unseen.
Gifted.
But ignored.
Trying.
But forgotten.
Yet the hidden place became David’s training ground.
The Psalms were not born in crowds.
They were born in isolation.
The secret place formed the public anointing.
In Matthew 6:6, Jesus says:
“But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who is unseen.”
The Greek phrase “close the door” includes the concept of shutting out distractions, separating from public visibility.
Because intimacy with God grows where performance dies.
Some believers are frustrated because their life feels hidden.
But hidden does not mean abandoned.
Seeds are hidden before harvest.
Roots are hidden before fruit.
Jesus spent roughly 30 years in obscurity before three years of ministry.
Thirty years hidden.
The Son of God.
Hidden.
What makes us think we are above hidden seasons?
God often conceals people before He reveals them.
Because hiddenness protects immature character from premature exposure.
The world celebrates visibility.
But heaven develops depth.
There are people reading this who feel forgotten.
You keep praying.
Keep serving.
Keep obeying.
But nothing seems to change.
Listen carefully:
Just because nobody sees your obedience does not mean heaven ignores it.
God develops roots in private before He trusts branches in public.
And send this to someone who feels invisible right now.
3. God Breaks Pride Before He Releases Influence
Pride is spiritual poison.
And the terrifying thing about pride is that proud people rarely realize they are proud.
Sometimes pride wears insecurity.
Sometimes pride sounds humble.
Sometimes pride cries during worship.
Lucifer fell because of pride.
Nebuchadnezzar lost his mind because of pride.
Peter denied Jesus because confidence in self collapsed under pressure.
God cannot safely elevate people who secretly worship themselves.
Proverbs 16:18 says:
“Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.”
The Hebrew word for pride here is:
גָּאוֹן (ga’on)
Meaning arrogance, self-exaltation, inflated importance.
And yet modern culture trains believers to build brands instead of carrying crosses.
We are living in an era where many people want influence more than holiness.
Visibility more than surrender.
Followers more than fruit.
But God is not impressed by charisma.
He watches character.
One of the greatest acts of mercy God can give a person is humiliation before elevation.
Because private breaking prevents public destruction.
Peter is a painful example.
Before becoming a pillar of the Church, he was shattered.
Jesus warned him in Luke 22:31:
“Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you as wheat.”
The Greek word for sift is:
σινιάζω (siniazō)
Meaning to violently shake through a sieve.
To separate.
To expose.
Peter thought he was stronger than he really was.
And God allowed the shaking to reveal it.
Some of you are offended by the season you are in.
But what if God is allowing your confidence in yourself to collapse so dependence on Him can finally grow?
Brokenness is not always punishment.
Sometimes it is preparation.
Because people who have never been broken often become dangerous when elevated.
Broken people tend to carry compassion.
Humility.
Mercy.
Tenderness.
The kind of depth success alone can never produce.
4. God Tests Obedience When Nobody Understands
Real obedience becomes visible when instructions stop making sense.
Abraham was told to leave his homeland.
Noah built an ark before rain existed.
Joshua marched around walls.
Hosea married a broken woman.
Mary carried a scandal before carrying a Savior.
And Jesus carried a cross before wearing a crown.
Biblical obedience has never looked logical to spectators.
That is why many people around you may misunderstand your season.
They cannot see what God told you privately.
In Genesis 22, Abraham is tested with Isaac.
The Hebrew phrase in Genesis 22:1 says:
וְהָאֱלֹהִים נִסָּה אֶת־אַבְרָהָם (Veha’Elohim nissah et-Avraham)
“God tested Abraham.”
Again the word:
נִסָּה (nissah)
To prove. To refine. To reveal faithfulness.
Many believers want elevation without tests.
But trust without testing remains theoretical.
Obedience costs something.
Sometimes comfort.
Sometimes relationships.
Sometimes reputation.
Sometimes certainty.
The terrifying thing about obedience is that God often gives enough light for the next step… but not the whole map.
And that uncertainty forces dependence.
Some of you are in a season where obeying God feels lonely.
You are trying to honor Christ while others compromise.
Trying to stay pure while culture mocks conviction.
Trying to trust God while prayers seem delayed.
Do not confuse difficulty with abandonment.
God often tests obedience before releasing assignment.
Because elevation without obedience creates rebellion with influence.
And heaven refuses to empower what has not surrendered.
5. God Allows Crushing Before Oil Flows
Olives are crushed before oil emerges.
And spiritually… many believers are asking God why life feels crushing.
But crushing often precedes anointing.
Jesus Himself entered Gethsemane before Calvary.
The name Gethsemane comes from the Aramaic/Hebrew concept:
גַּת שְׁמָנִים (gat shemanim)
“Oil press.”
Think about that.
Before the Cross… Jesus entered the crushing place.
Luke records that His sweat became like drops of blood.
The pressure was unbearable.
Yet surrender emerged there.
“Not my will, but Yours be done.”
Many believers want resurrection power without Gethsemane surrender.
But crushing reveals what comfort conceals.
When life breaks apart… what comes out of you?
Bitterness?
Rage?
Pride?
Or deeper dependence on God?
Some of the most anointed people carry deep scars.
Because suffering has a way of producing compassion.
Depth.
Authority.
Sensitivity to God.
Second Corinthians 4:8-9 says:
“We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed…”
The Greek language here paints the image of severe pressure without total destruction.
Pressed.
But preserved.
Afflicted.
But sustained.
Some of you feel emotionally exhausted.
You smile publicly while privately asking God how much more you can endure.
And maybe nobody around you fully understands the warfare happening in your mind.
But hear this clearly:
God does not waste crushing seasons.
Oil is expensive because crushing is painful.
There are dimensions of intimacy with God that only emerge through suffering.
Not because God enjoys your pain.
But because suffering often dismantles illusions.
And desperate people learn how to cling to Jesus differently.
Someone reading this needs to know they are not alone.
6. God Teaches You to Carry Glory Without Stealing It
Perhaps the most dangerous moment in a believer’s life is not failure.
It is success.
Because success reveals what failure never could.
Some people stay dependent on God when desperate.
But drift from Him once elevated.
That is why God teaches surrendered people how to carry influence without worshipping themselves.
In John 3:30, John the Baptist says:
“He must increase, but I must decrease.”
The Greek word for increase is:
αὐξάνω (auxanō)
To grow. To enlarge. To expand.
And “decrease” is:
ἐλαττόω (elattoō)
To become less. To lower oneself.
True elevation in the Kingdom is not self-exaltation.
It is greater surrender.
The greatest leaders in Scripture carried deep awareness that the glory belonged to God.
Moses fell on his face.
Isaiah cried “Woe is me.”
Paul called himself chief among sinners.
The closer people truly get to God, the less impressed they become with themselves.
And maybe that is the final lesson before elevation.
Learning that influence is stewardship.
Not ownership.
Gift.
Not entitlement.
Assignment.
Not identity.
Some of you are frustrated because life feels delayed.
But heaven is preparing your soul to survive what you are praying for.
Because platforms reveal character.
Visibility amplifies weakness.
Influence magnifies integrity problems.
And God loves you too much to elevate you prematurely.
The process hurts.
But it protects.
The waiting hurts.
But it develops.
The breaking hurts.
But it purifies.
And one day you may realize the season you begged God to end was actually the season that saved your future.
Be honest. This hit harder than you expected.
Because some people are not being punished.
They are being prepared.
And never forget this:
God often hides people before He elevates them because roots must become deeper than applause.
